adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Early-onset familial hypertension with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis plus simultaneously suppressed renin and aldosterone localizes the defect downstream of aldosterone to autonomous distal sodium reabsorption; Liddle syndrome is caused by ENaC gain of function.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Primary hyperaldosteronism requires inappropriate aldosterone excess, whereas this stem explicitly has low aldosterone. Bartter defects waste salt and raise renin/aldosterone. Direct ENaC gain of function uniquely explains the stated phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The strongest rejection argument would be another low-renin/low-aldosterone mineralocorticoid-like disorder, but the answer set asks for a transport abnormality and only constitutively increased ENaC directly matches Liddle syndrome.
